messages:
maria: Heads-up: hit a regression in the onboarding sample app where rapid client retries + a flaky SW cause duplicate Stripe charges on 429s. Repro on Chrome with fast reloads.

maria: Quick repro: click purchase -> SW intercepts POST /v1/checkout -> server sends 429 + small Retry-After -> client retries immediately (no backoff) -> server accepts on second request but SW replayed the original fetch too -> two charges.

kevin: That's nasty. Did the sample app use the browser SDK retry helper?

maria: It used the SDK wrapper but the sample's fetch wrapper treated 429 the same as network errors and retried synchronously. The SDK let the app override defaultRetry, and sample set it to true.

devon: Current SDK behavior: server SDKs auto-insert Idempotency-Key; browser SDK doesn't because of storage constraints and cross-tab concerns. We assumed browser flows use the app to handle side-effects. Clearly that's brittle.

sanjay: Two orthogonal fixes: 1) reduce surface of unsafe retries in sample apps (stop retrying on 429 unless idempotency key present); 2) enhance JS SDK with optional in-memory replay-guard + SW hooks.

alex: Concrete JS SDK plan: - default retry policy: exponential backoff (base 150ms) with full jitter, cap 5 retries - always respect Retry-After header when present - if payload looks side-effecting (heuristic: contains payment/webhook flags) and no Idempotency-Key, do NOT auto-retry 429s, bubble up error - provide opt-in auto-idempotency: SDK can create a UUID and attach Idempotency-Key header (configurable).

kevin: For SWs we could expose API so the worker can check sdk.inFlight(idempKey) before replaying. That requires coordinated storage; we can do BroadcastChannel or IndexedDB. BroadcastChannel is simpler but only works same-origin real-time.

maria: For a short-term patch I disabled retries on 429 in the sample app and re-ran tests — no duplicate charges. I'll open PR for that immediately.

devon: UX question: if SDK auto-generates Idempotency-Key, apps might expect deterministic de-dup behavior across tabs. We can't guarantee that for ephemeral in-memory keys. Need doc and naming: auto-idempotency vs persistent-idempotency.

sanjay: Implementation details: - generate idemp: uuidv4() when auto-idempotency enabled - keep an LRU set of recent keys (TTL 45s) to dedupe within same page - export peekInFlight(key) and onInFlight(key, cb) for SW integration - respect an environment flag SKIP_AUTO_IDEMPOTENCY for apps that manage keys server-side.

alex: Pseudocode for Retry-After parsing and backoff:```js
const ra = parseInt(res.headers.get('Retry-After') || '', 10);
const wait = Number.isFinite(ra) ? ra*1000 : Math.random()*Math.min(1000, base*Math.pow(2,attempt));
await sleep(wait);
```

kevin: Also add telemetry: emit event when SDK attaches an idempotency key and when it suppresses a retry due to missing key. That'll help support diagnose. Respect privacy flags though.

maria: Good call. Also add a debug env var so we can log decisions in dev: REDWOOD_JS_SDK_RETRY_DEBUG=true.

devon: Docs checklist: onboarding page note about browser vs server idempotency, SW snippet showing BroadcastChannel dedupe example, and a sample patch for the onboarding sample app. I'll own writing those.

ci-bot: build #4890 queued for branch fix/onboarding-retries (unit + integration).

sanjay: I'll prototype the SDK hooks this sprint. Plan: small opt-in feature behind a flag so we can roll out and iterate.

maria: Thanks everyone. Once PRs land we'll run a quick e2e with Stripe test mode and the SW repro to verify.
